svg.aria-label: Decision tree for choosing between the ordinal chain, the discrete hazard model and survival alternatives, based on whether the horizon is bounded by the grace period
svg.text: WHICH MODEL, AND WHEN
The question is not accuracy. All of these score within 0.02 PR-AUC. The question is whether your horizon is bounded.
Does anything you care about happen
after the grace period ends?
no
yes, revivals matter
ORDINAL CHAIN (the default)
The horizon is closed at day 45, so there is nothing to censor,
provided you train only on cohorts where grace has fully elapsed.
labels.mature() enforces that. Skip it and every recent due looks
like a lapse, which is the most expensive silent bug here.
Brier 0.0761, PR-AUC 0.3804, 12s to fit.
DISCRETE HAZARD
Payments landing 3, 6 or 12 months late make the horizon open
ended and the recent cohorts genuinely censored rather than bad.
It also stops you discarding them: a 20-day-old due contributes
20 days of exposure and is censored after.
Weak inside grace (weekly periods blur the day-45 edge), well
calibrated on revival at 28 / 42 / 91 / 182 / 364 days.
Cox PH, XGBoost AFT, mixture cure
A mixture cure model is the formal version of the two-stage idea. On tabular
data with this many categoricals, boosted trees beat Cox, and AFT cannot
represent a spike at day 0 and another at the deadline (mlogloss 1.53 vs 1.11).
Keep logistic regression in the registry forever
It posted the highest AUC in the table and fits in 2 seconds. When a boosted
model cannot beat that by a meaningful margin, you have learned something
about your features, not about your algorithm. Ship the challenger anyway.
